scenario: Hypertension review with ankle swelling that may be a side effect of amlodipine.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Good afternoon, Rajan. Take a seat. Did you find parking all right?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Good afternoon, doctor. Parking was a problem as usual, I had to leave the car on the main road. And this weather, so hot!

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Yes, it is very hot. So, how have you been since your last visit?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Mostly fine, doctor. I have come for my blood pressure review. And my ankles have been swelling a little.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Since when is the swelling there?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: About two weeks, I would say. Mostly in the evening.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Is it both legs? Any chest pain, breathlessness or fainting?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Both legs. No chest pain, no fainting, nothing like that. And no breathlessness.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Good. Which medicine are you taking for the pressure?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Amlokind, five milligrams, one tablet in the morning. I started a new strip, a different company, um, about three weeks ago. So it could be the new tablets, no?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Possibly. Amlodipine can cause some ankle swelling, whichever brand it is. Any other conditions, or operations in the past?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ten years of pressure. And I had my gallbladder removed in 2015. Nothing else.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Does anyone in your family have heart trouble or stroke?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: My father had a stroke when he was seventy.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Let me check your pressure now. It is 146 over 92, a bit high. Pulse is 80.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Is that bad, doctor? My home machine showed one forty most days.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Let me look at your legs. There is mild pitting swelling around both ankles. Your heart sounds are normal.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor, will I have to take these tablets for the whole life?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Most people with pressure do need long term treatment, but we can adjust it. I will reduce the amlodipine to two and a half milligrams and add telmisartan 40 milligrams in the morning.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay. Any tests?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I would like an ECG today, and a urine test and a kidney function test, since there is swelling.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: And what about food?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Cut down on salt, avoid pickles and papad, and walk for thirty minutes daily. Keep your legs up in the evening. Check the pressure at home every morning and bring the readings. Review me in two weeks with the reports.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Alright, I will do that. Thank you, doctor.

gold.key: mild pitting swelling around both ankles
reduce the amlodipine to two and a half milligrams
keep your legs up in the evening

notes: Parking and hot-weather small talk in turns 0 to 2 are unlabelled. Turn 7 is the explicit denial of red flags (no chest pain, no fainting, no breathlessness), labelled as negated symptoms and not as red_flag. Turn 9 contains the patient's own hedged guess that the new tablets might be the cause (labelled as an uncertain patient_concern). Turn 15 (home machine showed one forty) is a patient-reported reading and is deliberately NOT labelled vital_sign, since vital_sign is for measurements the doctor states aloud. The patient takes amlodipine (as amlokind); the doctor adds a different drug, telmisartan.
